newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugoslavia return to IMF key to more trade with UK.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslavia return to IMF key to more trade with UK.

text.p: A visiting British business delegation said on Wednesday it recognised opportunities for expanding cooperation with Yugoslavia but said major deals depended on the country's return to world financial bodies.

"The outer wall of sanctions does not limit normal trade but it is a barrier for large projects. The whole financial situation in terms of credit relations and payment terms is not easy," Robert Cardwell, head of the British mission visiting Belgrade, told reporters.
Cardwell said some deals have already been struck, but declined to give any details.

Cardwell, Vice President of the London Chamber of Commerce and Industry, cited the recent sale of a 49-percent stake in Serbia's Telekom as a good example of encouraging investors to take more interest in what is going on in Yugoslavia.
He was speaking after two-day talks organised between Yugoslav officials and firms and 20 British companies.

Yugoslalvia is seeking to be reintegrated in international bodies like the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Trade Organization (WTO). The United States kept an outer wall of sanctions on Belgrade after the U.N. lifted a trade embargo imposed on Serbia in 1992 for its role in the Bosnian war.
"There is an anticipation these barriers will be removed in the not too distant future, but we have to wait and see and hope for the best," Cardwell said.
"All the building blocks are in place, the legislation is there and there are no barriers to investment, to cooperation, to joint venture," Cardwell said.

Serbia was seen as a large market of more than 10 million consumers and an economy which has undergone some difficulties but the potential was there, he said. He added that British firms were interested in large infrastructure projects when the economic situation allowed it.
David Slim of the British embassy saw interesting opportunities in the food industry and agriculture, power production, oil and gas industries.
Cardwell called on Yugoslavia to take an initiative because it would face difficulties in regaining old markets and finding new ones now that new competitors have appeared in the last five years.
"It's not incumbent only on one player, you need the Yugoslav companies also to take the initiative and approach the right people. Yugoslavia has to sell itself more and again," he said.

Serbia and Montenegro need massive capital injections and the governments would decide individually on their strategic partners according to their initiative, Cardwell said. -- Beti Bilandzic, Belgrade newsroom 381 11 222 43 05
